<head-word>קִרְטֵעַ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (
<italic>Parel</italic> of קָטַע) [
<italic>to cut</italic>; cmp. גּוּז,] 
<italic>to caper, leap</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 38 ארכיליסטיס מְקַרְטֵעַ Ar. the chief robber (Satan) cuts his capers (ed. השטן מקטרג). Ib. s. 74 מְקַרְטְעִים בו Var., v. קִרְקֵר II. Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 19 נוער כשהוא מְקַרְטֵעַ (read: נראה) appearing as if it (the golden calf) were leaping, v. רָטַט. Ḥull. 75
<sup>a</sup> דג מקרטע (Ms. H. המִתְקַרְטֵעַ; Ms. R. 1 המקורטע; 2 המטרטע corr. acc.; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 2) a fish jumping (in the death agony); a. e.—Pesik. R. s. 40 [read:] שלא נראה המאכלת בא(ה) עלי ונְקַרְטֵעַ ונִיפָּסֵל וכ' lest we (I) see the knife coming on me, and make a convulsive movement, and become unfit for a sacrifice; [Friedm. corrects: שלא אראה … וַאֲקַרְטֵעַ ואִיפָּסֵל lest I see the knife &c.]</notes></sense></senses>

<entry id="S02018">
<head-word>קרי</head-word>
<head-word>קָרָא</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to call, name; to invite</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 7
<sup>b</sup> מיום שברא … שקְרָאוֹ … וּקְרָאוֹ אדון from the day that the Lord created the world there was no man that called the Holy One, blessed be He, lord, until Abraham came and called him lord (Gen. XV, 2 אדני). Gen. R. s. 56 אברהם קראו יראה Abraham called it (the Temple site) 
<italic>yeraëh</italic> (Gen. XXII, 14), שם ק' אותו שלם Shem called it Salem (ib. XIV, 18), הריני קוֹרֵא אותו ירושלם I will call it Jerusalem. Snh. 70
<sup>b</sup> אין … לִקְרוֹא אבא וכ' no sooner does a child know to call ‘father’ and ‘mother’, than it tastes grain food. Num. R. s. 15, beg. ק' אותו אוהב he invited that friend. Ib. והיה קורא אומניות, v. אוּמָנוּת; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. קָרוּא, קָרוּי; f. קְרוּאָה, קְרוּיָה; 
<plural-form>Pl. קְרוּאִים, קְרוּאִין, קְרוּיִים, קְרוּיִם, קְרוּיִין, קְרוּיִן; קְרוּאוֹת, קְרוּיוֹת</plural-form>. B. Mets. 114
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. (ref. to Ez. XXXIV, 31) אתם ק' אדם וכ' you are called men, but idolaters &c. Sifra Aḥăré, end כל העריות ק' טומאה all illicit connections are called uncleanness; a. fr.—Esp. קְרוּאִים, קְרוּיִין 
<italic>those called up to read from the Torah</italic> (v. infra). Gen. R. s. 70 (ref. to Gen. XXIX, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> אלו שלשה ק' this is typical of the three persons called up to read from the Torah (priest, Levite, and Israelite).</definition>
<notes> Y. Meg. III, 74
<sup>b</sup> ולא שבעה ק' אינון are not seven persons called up (on the Sabbath)?; a. fr.—V. קְרוּיוֹת.—2) 
<italic>to read, recite</italic> (esp. from the Scriptures). Yoma I, 6 אם רגיל לִקְרוֹת … קוֹרִין לפניו if he (the high priest) is accustomed to read (the Scriptures), he reads himself, if not, they read to him; ובמה קורין לפניו and from what books do they read to him? Ib. פעמים הרבה קָרִיתִי וכ' many a time I read to him from Daniel. Meg. II, 1 הקורא את המגילה וכ', v. מִפְרֵעַ. Ib. 2 קְרָאָהּ סירוגין, v. סֵירוּג. Ib. 3 קורא כמקומו he must read in accordance with the usage of the place he came from. Ib. 4 הכל כשרין לִקְרוֹת וכ' all persons are qualified to recite the Book of Esther (before the congregation). Y. Meg. IV, 74
<sup>d</sup> bot. וקְרָיָיהּ and read from it; a. fr.—Esp. 
<italic>to read from the Torah</italic> at public services. Ib. III, 4 קורין בפרשת שקלים they (those who are called up, v. supra) read the section of Sheḳalim (Ex. XXX, 11-16). Ib. 6 אחד קורא את כולן one person must read the entire chapter (of the curses). Ib. IV, 1 בשני … קורין שלשה on Mondays … three persons read. Ib. 4 הקורא בתורה לא יפחות וכ' he who is designated to read from the Torah must read no less than three verses; לא יִקְרָא למתורגמן וכ' he must read to the interpreter one verse at a time, but from the Prophets, three verses. Bicc. I, 1 יש מביאין … וקורין וכ' there are those who are bound to bring the first-fruits and to read (Deut. XXVI, 5-10), and those who must bring but not read &c. Ib. 4; a. v. fr.—Esp. (את שמע) ק' 
<italic>to recite the Sh’mʿa</italic> in the morning and in the evening prayer. Ber. I, 1 לא קָרִינוּ וכ' we omitted to read the Sh’mʿa. Ib. II, 3 ק' וטעה if one read the Sh’mʿa and made a mistake. Ib. 4 האומנין קוֹרְאִין וכ' (Bab. ed. 16
<sup>a</sup> קורין) workingmen read the Sh’mʿa on top of a tree, or on the scaffolding; a. v. fr.—אל תִּקְרֵי … אלא (or תִּיקְרִי Chald. 
<pgbrk id="pg1418" />form; abbrev. א"ת) read not … but—, i.e. change the traditional (Massoretic) reading (for homiletical purposes). Ib. 64
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Is. LIV, 13 א"ת בָּנַיִךְ אלא בּוֹנַיִךְ read not 
<italic>banayikh</italic> (thy children) but 
<italic>bonayikh</italic> (thy builders, the scholars). M. Kat. 9
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Ps. XLIX, 12) א"ת קִרְבָּם אלא קִבְרָם read not 
<italic>ḳirbam</italic> (their innermost) but 
<italic>ḳibram</italic> (their grave); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קֵרֵא</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same, 
<italic>to call, invite</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Part. pass. מְקוֹרָא, 
<plural-form>pl. מְקוֹרָאִים, מְקוֹרָאִין</plural-form>. Num. R. s. 13 יש חתן … למק' וכ' does a bridegroom give a banquet for the invited guests and not sit with them?; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִקְרָא</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be called</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lev. R. s. 1, beg. נִקְרְאוּ הנביאים וכ', v. בַּיִת. Ex. R. s. 1 (ref. to Ex. II, 13) מכאן … נ' רשע from here we learn that when a man lifts up his hand to strike his neighbor, even if he does not strike, he is called a wicked man; Snh. 58
<sup>b</sup>. Ab. Zar. 19
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Ps. I, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> בתחלה נִקְרֵאת … נקראת וכ' first it (the Law) is called the Lord’s, and then his (the student’s); a. fr.— 
<italic>to be read, recited</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Meg. I, 1 מגלה נקראת וכ' the Book of Esther may be read at public service on the eleventh &c. Ib. IV, 10 מעשה ראובן נ' ולא וכ' the story of Reuben (Gen. XXXV, 22) is read at public service but not translated. Ib. לא נִקְרָאִין וכ' (Y. ed. נִיקְרִין) must be neither read nor interpreted. Tosef. ib. IV (III), 31 יש נקראין ומתרגמין וכ' certain verses are read but not interpreted &c.; Meg. 25
<sup>a</sup> נִקְרִין; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִקְרִיא</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cause to call, to lead in reading</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sot. 10
<sup>a</sup> sq. (ref. to Gen. XXI, 33) א"ת וַיִּקְרָא אלא וַיַּקְרִיא read not 
<italic>vayiḳra</italic> (and he called) but 
<italic>vayaḳri</italic> (and he made call), מלמד שה' וכ' intimating that Abraham caused the name of the Lord to be called by the mouth of every passer-by. Y. ib. V, 20
<sup>c</sup> top קטן שהוא מַקְרֵא וכ' a child that reads the Hallel at school, and they (the class) respond by repeating each sentence (v. עָנָה I); גדול שהוא מקרא וכ' an adult that leads in reciting …, when the congregation responds with the first sentence (as refrain). Succ. III, 10 מי שהיה … מַקְרִין אותו וכ' if a slave, a woman, or a child reads to him, he responds with Hallelujah. Gitt. III, 1 שמע קול סופרים מקרין וכ' heard the teaching scribes as they made the practicing children read, ‘such and such … divorces &c.’—Esp. 
<italic>to teach the Scriptures</italic> (מִקְרָא). Lam. R. to I, 6 הַקְרינִי דף אחד … השניני וכ' teach me a page of the Scriptures, teach me a chapter of the Mishnah; a. fr.—[Erub. 104
<sup>b</sup> שהקרו, v. קָרַר I.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S02019">
<head-word>קְרֵי</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<head-word>קְרָא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>to call, name, invite</italic>; 
<italic>to read</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XXIX, 34. Targ. I Sam. III, 6. Targ. Gen. II, 19, sq. Targ. Deut. XVII, 19. Targ. Esth. VI, 1; a. v. fr.—Meg. 18
<sup>b</sup> דקָרוּ ליה וכ' when they call him (in his sleep), and he answers. Gen. R. s. 17; Lev. R. s. 34 קְרוּן בשכונתיה וכ' they called (begging for alms) in the neighborhood &c. Ber. 13
<sup>b</sup> מִקְרָא הוא דלא לִיקְרֵי וכ' one is not permitted to read the Sh’mʿa (while lying on one’s back), but &c.; מקרא … נמי אסיר to read is forbidden even when turning sideways. Ib. 11
<sup>b</sup> כתיב רע וקְרִינָן הכל it is written (Is. XLV, 7) ‘and creates 
<italic>evil</italic>’, and we read (in the morning prayers) ‘
<italic>all</italic>’! Pes. 3
<sup>a</sup> קָרוּ נגהי, v. נָגְהָא. Ib. קַרְיֵיה … לנהורא וכ' the Lord called the light and appointed it &c. Gen. R. s. 40 הוה קָרֵי עליהין נותן וכ' applied to them the verse (Is. XL, 29), he giveth &c. M. Kat. 5
<sup>b</sup> top, a. fr. ק' עליה וכ' applied to him the verse &c. Keth. 17
<sup>a</sup> sq. למאן דקרי ותני וכ' (at the funeral) of one that read the Bible and studied Mishnah, but of one that taught others &c. Sabb. 152
<sup>b</sup> גלית … נביאי לא קְרֵית thou showest that thou hast not even read the Prophets (v. infra). Y. Meg. III, 74
<sup>b</sup> bot. אילין … מאי דיִקְרִינָן וכ' as to the curses (v. אֲרַר), dare one person read them and recite the benediction before and after them? Ex. R. s. 47 למדו … ודקָרִין בלילה learn the Torah from such teachers as get up early and study while it is yet night, v. אִימְּטִין; a. v. fr.—Y. Meg. IV, 75
<sup>a</sup> bot., a. e. קְרָאיֵי they recite.—Part. pass. קְרִי, קְרִיא; 
<plural-form>pl. קְרִיָּין</plural-form>
<italic>the Massoretic reading</italic>, opp. כתיב. Treat. Sof’rim ch. IX, 8. Ned. 37
<sup>b</sup>, v. כְּתִיב; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַקְרֵי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (

<italic>horn, trump, wind instrument</italic>. Kel. XI, 7 ק' עגולה a round (wound) metal horn; contrad. to פשוטה a plain (straight) horn; Sabb. 47
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—

<plural-form>pl. קְרָנִים, קְרָנִין, קְרָנוֹת</plural-form>. Tosef. Par. II (I), 2; Bekh. 44

XXXIII, 17), and that one (Rome) is &c. (Dan. VII, 24). Y. Shek. VI, 50
<sup>a</sup> top כקַרְנֵי וכ', v. כִּילּוּיָא. Ib.; Yoma 77

<number>—2)</number>

<italic>corner</italic>, v. זָוִית. Ber. 17

<entry id="S02128">
<head-word>קָרַע</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to tear, split</italic>; esp. 
<italic>to rend the garment in mourning</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kel. XVI, 5 עד שיִקְרְעֶנּוּ (Mish. ed. שיַקְרִיעֶנּוּ 
<italic>Hif.</italic>) until he tears the bale open. M. Kat. 22
<sup>b</sup> על כל … אינו קוֹרֵעַ אלא עליון for all dead (except parents) … one must rend only the upper garment. Ib. האשה קוֹרַעַת וכ' a woman (mourning for her parents) rends the lower garment and puts it back in its place, and then rends the upper garment. Snh. 60
<sup>a</sup> אחד השומע … חייב לִקְרוֹעַ both he that hears a blasphemy directly, and he that hears it from one that heard it (and reports as witness before court) must rend his garment; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. קָרוּעַ; 
<plural-form>pl. קְרוּעִים, קְרוּעִין</plural-form>. M. Kat. 26
<sup>b</sup> היוצא בבגד ק' וכ' he that marches before a corpse with a garment rent (for a previous case) robs (deceives) the dead and the living. Ib.
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to II Kings II, 12) ק' ועומדים לשנים remaining always rent in two; ib. 22
<sup>b</sup> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 4); Snh. l. c.; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קֵרֵעַ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same. M. Kat. 26 same.</definition>
<notes> M. Kat. 26
<sup>b</sup> ואין מְקָרְעִין בפניו you must not rend your garment in his (the sick man’s) presence. Ib. מקרעין לקטן וכ' we rend a minor’s garment in order to make him feel sad; ib. 14
<sup>b</sup>. R. Hash. 16
<sup>b</sup> ארבעה … מקרעין גזר וכ' four things cause an evil decree passed on man to be torn (cancelled), they are: charity, prayer &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (cmp. גָּרַע) 
<italic>to scrape, to mark the outlines of letters by abrasion</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 19
<sup>b</sup> עדים … מקרעין להם וכ' for witnesses that know not how to sign their names, grooves are made on blank paper, and they fill the grooves out with ink; ib. 9
<sup>b</sup>; Y. ib. II, 44
<sup>b</sup> top ומְקָרֵעַ; [Tosaf. to Gitt. 9
<sup>b</sup>: you cut the names out on blank paper and put it on the document, and the witnesses fill the cuts out]. Tosef. Sabb. XI (XII), 8, contrad. fr. רשם; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִקְרַע</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be torn; to be cut open, be operated upon by a section</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. VIII, 6, a. e. טומטום שנ', v. טוּמְטוּם. Bekh. 42
<sup>b</sup> שמא יִקָּרֵעַ וכ' he may have an operation performed, and be found a eunuch; Tosef. Yeb. XI, 1; Yeb. 83
<sup>b</sup>. B. Bath. 168
<sup>b</sup> נ' פסול נִתְקָרֵעַ כשר if a document is found torn, it is invalid; if it appears torn by accident, it is valid as evidence; ib. נ' קֶרַע של בית דין נתק' וכ' 
<italic>miḳrʿa</italic> refers to the rent as made in court for cancellation, 
<italic>nithḳareʿa</italic> refers to a rent different from the manner customary in court; Y. Gitt. II, 44
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְקָרֵעַ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to become torn</italic>, v. supra.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<plural-form>Pl. קְרָעִים, קְרָעִין</plural-form>. Ib. 26
<sup>a</sup> ואלו ק' שאין וכ' and these are the rents which must never be stitched together. Sifra Thazr. Par. 5, ch. XVI (ref. to Lev. XIII, 57) לימד על כל הק' וכ' this shows that all the torn-off pieces must be burnt. Snh. 60

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Parel of קפף, cmp. נָקַף II Hif.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>enclosure, esp. an enclosed space outside of a settlement</italic>, for storage of wood &c. Erub. II, 3 לא אמרו … לגנה ולק' they limited the area to two S’ahs only for a garden and a storehouse.</definition>
<notes> Ib. 5 הגינה והק' שהן וכ' a garden or a 
<italic>ḳarpif</italic> of seventy (cubits) and a fraction by seventy and a fraction, surrounded by a fence ten handbreadths high &c. Bets. IV, 2 מביאין … ומן הק' וכ' you may bring in (on the Holy Day for immediate use) wood from the field, taking from what is piled up, and from the 
<italic>k</italic>. even from what lies around scattered; איזהו ק' כל וכ' what is understood by 
<italic>k</italic>.? An enclosed space near the town. B. Bath. 24
<sup>b</sup> ק' … שהוקף לדירה a 
<italic>ḳ</italic>.… which has been enclosed 
<pgbrk id="pg1425" />for living purposes; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>an area</italic> (of seventy square cubits) 
<italic>outside of a town, added to the city limits for the purposes of Sabbath distances</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Erub. V, 2 נותנין ק' לעיר for measuring Sabbath limits we allow a 
<italic>ḳ</italic>. to each town; וחכמים … ק' אלא בין וכ' but the scholars say, a 
<italic>ḳ</italic>. as an extension to city limits is allowed only in the case of two neighboring towns; אם יש לזו … עושה ק' לשתיהן להיותן כאחת (Y. ed. קִרְפּוּף) if there is a space of seventy cubits for one and an equal space for the other, this forms a 
<italic>ḳ</italic>. for both, so that they may be considered as one town. Ib. 57
<sup>a</sup> מאי ק' תורת ק' by 
<italic>ḳ</italic>. the scholars mean the application of the law of 
<italic>ḳ</italic>. (as an extension to the town); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קַרְפִּיפוֹת</plural-form>. Ib. IX, 1 אחד גגות … ק' רשות וכ' joint roofs, courts, and enclosures are each considered as one area (for Sabbath movements). Ib. 89
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> קרקסאיות Ar. (ed. קרקייאות, corr. acc.), v. פָּקַח; Sabb. 150
<sup>a</sup> קרקסאות (Ms. O. קרקיסיאות). Gen. R. s. 67. Ib. s. 80 צריכין אנו … ולבתי ק' שלהם וכ' we must give credit to the nations that they bring actors to their theatres and circuses and amuse themselves with them, so that they may not talk with one another and come to vain quarrels. <sup>b</sup>) ואם היה (ב) מחובר לק' if the flax was bought while standing in the field, v. חָבַר. Ib. 4 הקונה שני … לא קנה ק' if a person buys two trees in a neighbor’s field, he has not bought the ground belonging thereto. Ib. בעל הק' the owner of the ground. Y. Succ. I, 51
<sup>d</sup> מן הק' from the floor of the Succah. Sifré Num. 126 קַרְקָעוֹ של בית וכ' the ground on which the house stands down to the deep; a. fr.—Snh. 74
<sup>b</sup> אסתר ק' עולם היתה Esther was merely like natural ground (that is ploughed), i.e. in submitting to the embraces of the heathen king she did no act on her part.—Esp. 
<italic>immovable property</italic>, opp. מְטַלְטְלִין. B. Mets. 11
<sup>b</sup> לקנות על גבי ק' to be acquired in connection with immovable property, v. אַגַּב. B. Bath. 156
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קַרְקָעוֹת</plural-form>. Y. ib. IX, 17

<sup>b</sup>, a. e. שעבוד ק', v. שִׁעְבּוּד; a. fr.—Tosef. Kel. B. Kam. VII, 15 קַרְקְעוֹת הכלים, v. קַרְקָרָה.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
